Between 1 and 20 owners. The schema macro has no item-count option for
arrays, so the count is enforced in `ApplicationsService::create`
(`MAX_OWNERS`), after the framework's 2 MiB body limit.

The only response that carries a full SSN. Issued by the audited

contract.name: Sign In
contract.summary: Verify email, password and (when enabled) a two-factor code; starts a session

totp.description: Six-digit authenticator code; required once two-factor sign-in is enabled.

contract.name: Sign Out
contract.summary: End the caller's session

contract.name: Current User
contract.summary: The signed-in user

contract.name: Start Two-Factor Enrolment
contract.summary: Issue a new authenticator secret for the caller

jsonSchema.title: MfaEnrolment
jsonSchema.description:
Returned once, when enrolment starts. The secret is stored encrypted and
only becomes active after `MfaCode` confirms the authenticator works.

contract.name: Confirm Two-Factor Enrolment
contract.summary: Turn two-factor sign-in on once a code from the authenticator verifies

contract.name: Change Password
contract.summary: Change the caller's own password; ends every session of the user and starts a new one

jsonSchema.title: ChangePassword
jsonSchema.description: A signed-in user changing their own password.

contract.name: Report Browser Error
contract.summary: Record an error the front end caught in the browser (class and stack frames only)

jsonSchema.title: BrowserErrorReport
jsonSchema.description:
One error the front end caught in a user's browser. It deliberately has no
field for the error message: messages can quote what a user typed.

screen.description: Screen it happened on, with record ids replaced, for example "#/applications/:id".

stack.description: Stack frames only: function, script file, line and column.

contract.name: Request Document Upload
contract.summary: Issue a grant to upload one PDF (20 MB at most) directly to object storage

jsonSchema.title: NewDocument
jsonSchema.description:
Step 1 of an upload: describe the file. The API answers with a short-lived
grant to send the bytes straight to object storage.

url.description:
POST a multipart form here: every entry of `fields`, then the file as
`file`. Where files travel through the API (`ClientSettingsResponse`), PUT the
PDF itself here instead; `fields` is then empty.

contract.name: Complete Document Upload
contract.summary: Confirm the stored file is a PDF within the size limit and queue figure extraction

contract.name: Download Document
contract.summary: Issue a short-lived download link; the download is audited

url.description: Short-lived link to the stored PDF.

contract.name: Read Document Content
contract.summary: Hosted demo only: the stored PDF itself; the download is audited

contract.name: Access Review
contract.summary: Every account with role, second factor, last sign-in and staleness, for the periodic access review

jsonSchema.title: AccessReview
jsonSchema.description:
Who has access, with which role, and when they last used it: what an admin
goes through at each periodic access review.

last_review_by.description: Id of the admin who recorded the last review.

review_overdue.description: No review has been recorded within `review_interval_days`.

truncated.description: True when there are more accounts than one report holds.

AccessReviewEntry.description: One account in the access review.

days_since_last_use.description: Whole days since the account was last used (sign-in, creation or re-enabling).

stale.description: Active, and unused for longer than `stale_after_days`.

contract.name: Record Access Review
contract.summary: Record in the audit trail that the caller reviewed the accounts as they are now

jsonSchema.title: AccessReviewRecorded
jsonSchema.description: The audit entry written when an admin records that the review was done.

contract.name: List Audit Log
contract.summary: One page of the append-only audit trail, newest first; x-next-cursor continues

AuditEntry.description:
One row of the append-only audit trail: who did what to which record, and
when. Rows hold identifiers and fixed action names, never record contents.

user_id.description: Who: the acting user's id. Absent for the scheduled jobs.

action.description: What: a fixed action name such as `ssn_revealed` or `user_role_changed`.

entity_id.description: Which record: the id of the application, owner, document or user.

detail.description: A fixed qualifier (the new role, the field that was read), never a value.

request_id.description: The request the entry was written in, to find it in the logs.
